title.narrative: Improve access to life-saving GBV response services to crisis-affected people in remote areas of Afdem and Gabalu Woredas, Somali Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtOWS Development Fund (OWS-DF), a national NGO with deep operational presence in Ethiopia’s Somali Region, proposes a lifesaving intervention to strengthen GBV response services in Afdem and Gabalu woredas of Sitti Zone. This project responds to alarming protection concerns identified in the January 2025 Multi-Indicator Rapid Assessment (MIRA), which documented over 80 conflict-related sexual violence cases and revealed that the vast majority of survivors lacked access to clinical, psychosocial, or legal support. Local health facilities were found to be critically under-resourced, and Women and Children’s Affairs offices faced severe capacity and resource limitations. GBV risks are further exacerbated by unsafe water access, economic instability, displacement, and the collapse of traditional protection systems.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis eight-month project seeks to provide holistic, survivor-centered GBV services to 9,941 people (59% female, 46% children), including 1,491 internally displaced persons, 199 returnees, and 7,973 host community members. The project will establish two Women and Girls Friendly Spaces (WGFS) to deliver safe, confidential, and inclusive access to case management, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Psychological First Aid (PFA), legal assistance, and emergency cash support. A total of 1,500 dignity kits will be distributed to address menstrual health and uphold the dignity of vulnerable women and girls. The project will train 60 frontline service providers including health workers, social workers, and legal focal points on Clinical Management of Rape (CMR), GBV case management, and referral protocols, ensuring safe and effective survivor-centered service delivery.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo foster community ownership and tackle stigma and harmful norms, OWS-DF will implement 10 structured awareness-raising sessions using Somali-language IEC materials. These sessions will engage traditional and religious leaders, youth groups, and women’s associations to promote behavioral change and increase understanding of GBV, survivors’ rights, and available services. In parallel, 10 community-based protection committees will be established, trained, and equipped with toolkits to support localized GBV monitoring and referral, strengthening grassroots protection capacity. The project will also support the establishment of inter-agency referral pathways through service mapping, coordination meetings, and dissemination of Somali-language referral directories.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtOWS-DF brings a strong presence and trusted relationships in the project area, particularly in Gabalu woreda, where it has successfully implemented a previous Health Cluster project. This presence facilitates deep community access, local partnerships, and a culturally informed approach to service delivery. An estimated 36,385 people will be indirectly reached through improved community awareness, enhanced protection infrastructure, and expanded access to information. Targeted investments in One-Stop Centers, feedback mechanisms, and localized complaint-handling systems will ensure accountability, build trust, and strengthen the humanitarian response. All activities are grounded in a survivor-centered, rights-based, and culturally sensitive approach, with emphasis on inclusion of persons with disabilities and other marginalized groups.lt/pgtltpgtThis project directly aligns with the Ethiopia Humanitarian Fund (EHF) 2025 strategic priorities by addressing urgent protection needs in hard-to-reach, underserved areas with no other GBV actors present. The USD 250,000 requested will enable OWS-DF to deliver timely, coordinated, and culturally appropriate protection services, reduce the risk of GBV, and restore dignity and resilience to the most vulnerable women and girls in Afdem and Gabalu.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
